expectations.text: Cites EDPB draft Guidelines 02/2026 on anonymisation (consultation open until October 30, 2026), replacing the 2014 WP29 opinion once final
expectations.evidence: Only "Guidelines 01/2025 on pseudonymisation" and anonymisation guidance "expected to follow" — draft Guidelines 02/2026 and the October 30 consultation deadline are not cited.

expectations.text: States the relative approach to identifiability per CJEU EDPS v SRB: the same dataset can be personal for one holder, anonymous for another
expectations.evidence: "SRB v EDPS (CJEU, C-413/23 P, September 2025): the Court endorsed a relative approach. Pseudonymised data may not be personal data for a recipient who cannot reasonably re-identify it... the assessment is from the recipient's perspective."

expectations.text: Applies the means-reasonably-likely test and the singling-out/linkability/inference criteria
expectations.evidence: "all the means reasonably likely to be used, such as singling out... considering cost, time required, available technology"; WP29 criteria "1. Singling out... 2. Linkability... 3. Inference."

expectations.text: Distinguishes pseudonymisation (still personal data) from anonymisation
expectations.evidence: "Removing names or direct identifiers is pseudonymisation, not anonymisation"; "treat the data as pseudonymised personal data and apply GDPR in full."

expectations.text: Gives practical guidance: document the re-identification risk assessment per recipient context; auxiliary data and key retention defeat anonymity claims
expectations.evidence: "Define the release context: who receives the data, what other data they hold or can access"; "Run a documented re-identification risk assessment"; "If the recipient has or can reasonably obtain the key, the data stays personal"; "Ignoring the controller's own ability to re-link."
